snapshot_warning: PHASE A SNAPSHOT, TAKEN WHILE A BATCH OF AGENTS IS PUSHING TO THIS REPOSITORY. This is a point-in-time record, not a deletion list. Do not act on it. Phase B must collect its own observations -- one immediately before the deletion and one immediately after -- with scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs, and authorize against those. authorizeDeletion performs that collection itself rather than accepting one, and the invariants are compared between the two fresh observations, never against this file. This baseline is historical context: the repository goes on moving, and a Phase B compared against a Phase A snapshot would report ordinary progress as damage.
method: Read-only, and every asserted derivation is a command run by scripts/collect-branch-state.mjs with its command line, exit code, byte count and a SHA-256 of its raw stdout recorded beside the answer. That includes the graph facts, not only the repository queries around them: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against dev and main, `git rev-list --count` in both directions and for commits reaching neither line, `git tag --contains`, `git grep` over the whole tree, `git log -1`, and an all-state `gh pr list --head` per branch. Head lists are taken over two independent transports and cross-checked. Every list endpoint is paginated to the end, and each GitHub-wide search records whether it retrieved every result the API reported -- a truncated sweep establishes nothing and says so. No ref was created, deleted, renamed or force-pushed to produce this file.

invariant_baseline.note: Historical context, not the deletion comparison. What must not change across a deletion is compared between two observations collected either side of it (boundaryInvariantFindings); this baseline records what Phase A saw so a later reader can see how far the repository has moved since.

revision_history.note: Schema v2: the six-value classification, release-tag containment, superseding evidence, the reference scan, protection status, and a named list of what could not be established.
Schema v3: external facts moved behind a receipted collector, the destructive decision took a live observation, and the Phase B deletion log stopped being emitted in Phase A.

Schema v4, closing the second enumerated review. The observation digest is now recursive: the previous one passed an array replacer to JSON.stringify, which is a key allowlist applied at every level, so every nested head, pull request and receipt hashed to the same value and the digest bound nothing. Every graph derivation a branch record asserts is now collected here with its own receipt -- previously the record asserted merge-base, rev-list, tag-contains, grep and PR-history results the collector never ran. List endpoints paginate to the end and searches prove completeness, so an open pull request on a second page can no longer read as absent. Calendar-impossible instants are rejected before any freshness arithmetic. The invariant comparison is now between two freshly collected observations bracketing the deletion instead of against this snapshot. And the after-snapshot head exception has to be earned by an open pull request rather than by appearing in a list.

unestablished.fact: what the branch was used to read, and whether anything was ever committed to it and later discarded
unestablished.searched: The receipted complete GitHub-wide sweep, a receipted `git grep` over the tree, and the receipted all-state PR history: nothing names it outside this audit, #572 and the previous audit's PR, and no pull request ever used it as a head. A remote branch has no reflog readable from a clone, so a commit pushed and force-replaced before this audit would leave no trace any command here can reach.
unestablished.why_it_does_not_bear: The question is about objects that are not on the ref now. The ref as it stands is an ancestor of both dev and main with 0 commits reaching neither, so deleting it removes no reachable object. An object already unreachable from this ref is not preserved by keeping the ref either, which is why #572 routes evidence into committed fixtures and issue records rather than leaving it on a branch.

branches.reason: Receipted derivations place the tip on both dev and main with 0 commits reaching neither line, and in release tags v0.1.16 and v0.1.17. It is the merge commit of PR #538 and the branch never advanced past it. It is a tmp/* branch, which repository policy caps at seven days or task end; it is past that. The all-state PR history is empty and the complete reference sweep finds nothing outside this audit.

lifecycle.note: The PR carrying this audit must not use a closing keyword for #572. It completes the read-only-audit phase; final-deletion is blocked on #578 and #588 and is the phase that produces the deletion log.

phase_b_contract.note: The Phase B output is `branch-deletion-log`, which the canonical execution plan reserves for the blocked final-deletion phase. No deletion log is emitted by this PR; what is recorded here is the contract that artifact has to satisfy.
phase_b_contract.prerequisite_authority: fixtures/execution-plan/github-state.json -- #578 and #588 must be closed there with close evidence. The deletion log does not clear its own prerequisites; scripts/branch-audit.mjs cross-checks its claims against that snapshot and treats a disagreement as a finding.
phase_b_contract.entry_point: authorizeDeletion({ audit, log, completion }) in scripts/branch-audit.mjs. It collects the pre-deletion observation itself rather than accepting one, so the observation is not a value the deleting party composes.

required_shape.deleted: [{name, sha}] -- exactly the branches a fresh audit finds eligible, each at the commit that audit judged. An empty list is legitimate when nothing is eligible, and then no_op_reason must say why.
required_shape.blockers_cleared: [{issue, canonical_state}] -- cross-checked against the canonical snapshot, not believed
required_shape.pre_observation: {digest} -- the recursive digest of the observation collected immediately before the deletion
required_shape.post_observation: {digest} -- the recursive digest of the observation collected immediately after it

phase_b_contract.invariant_comparison: boundaryInvariantFindings(log, pre, post): main, dev, tag ref and commit identity, the complete protection objects, the rulesets, the install source, the repository settings, and every open pull request head -- compared between the two fresh observations. The set of heads that vanished between them must equal exactly the set the log says it deleted.

repository_policy.note: The branch policy this issue asks to be written down. Descriptive of the repository's current settings where a setting exists, prescriptive where none does.
rules: feature/, task/ and fix/ branches are deleted once their PR merges. delete_branch_on_merge is enabled, so this happens automatically; the branches in this audit that were not removed are the ones that never had a PR.
tmp/* branches live at most seven days or until their task ends, whichever comes first. No setting enforces this; it is checked by re-running this audit.
release/ and hotfix/ branches are deleted after the release ships and the back-merge into dev lands.
main and dev are protected: no deletion, no force push, enforced for admins. No repository rulesets are configured.

A branch is not an evidence archive. Anything worth keeping is moved into a commit, a committed fixture, a document or an issue record before the branch it lived on is deleted -- which is why this issue's Phase B is blocked on #578 and #588 rather than running now.
